route-des-grandes-alpes-col-du-cormet-de.title: Route des Grandes Alpes: Col du Cormet de Roselend to Col du Galibier
route-des-grandes-alpes-col-du-cormet-de.slogan: Col du Cormet de Roselend to Col du Galibier, over 2764 m · one way, about 227 km back to the start

waypoints.name: Col du Cormet de Roselend
waypoints.advice: Col du Cormet de Roselend is where the day begins. Next is Col de l Iseran, climbing 797 m.

waypoints.name: Col de l Iseran
waypoints.advice: Col de l Iseran comes up 114 km in. The road climbs 797 m on the way up to it, steadily. Reckon on about 5 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Nothing on this route is higher. Next is Col du Galibier.

waypoints.name: Col du Galibier
waypoints.advice: The route ends here after 227 km. Reckon on about 4 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind.

sections.advice: Col du Cormet de Roselend → Col de l Iseran climbs about 797 m in 53 km. This is the part worth slowing down for - look through the bends and use the pull-offs.
Col de l Iseran → Col du Galibier is 78 km of getting across. Ride it tidily and keep the enthusiasm for what comes after.

route-des-grandes-alpes-col-du-cormet-de.provenance: CURATED FROM THE ARCHIVE: waypoints taken from the named road Route des Grandes Alpes. Distances between stops are great-circle with a road factor, not a routed measurement - the pipeline replaces them when it routes this line.

scenicChapters.title: Col du Cormet de Roselend → Col de l Iseran
scenicChapters.narrative: The ground tilts up and stays tilted for 92 km. 797 m of it, taken steadily rather than in one wall — a steady rhythm suits this better than bursts. The height arrives whether you hurry or not.

scenicChapters.title: Col de l Iseran → Col du Galibier
scenicChapters.narrative: Height already gained and held. The road stays near 2764 m for 135 km instead of surrendering it to the next valley. Exposed ground: wind matters more here than gradient. Nothing blocks it.

route-des-grandes-alpes-col-du-cormet-de.story: A one-way ride of 227 km, Beaufort to Valloire - roughly 3 h 13 in the saddle. The highest point is 2,764 m. Cormet de Roselend and Col du Galibier are subject to seasonal closure - check it is open before you set off. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.
